dedupe_keys.name: stress testing of liquidity risk in target2 ecb occasional paper 183

description: This case study reports a stress test of liquidity risk in TARGET2, the euro's real-time gross settlement payment system, which settled on average EUR 1,835 billion in 343,729 transactions a day in 2015. It was carried out by an ad hoc group of TARGET2 operators and overseers under the ECB's Market Infrastructure Board and published as ECB Occasional Paper 183 in February 2017. The scenarios apply extreme shocks to the value of different levels and types of collateral, which shrink the intraday credit lines and so the payment capacity of participants; the TARGET2 simulator replays real transaction-level data with the changed credit lines for one maintenance period in each year from 2008 to 2013. The paper is a free PDF from the ECB; the transaction data themselves are confidential. Caveats: the period was shaped by unconventional monetary policy with abundant liquidity, which the authors note, so results may be milder than in tighter conditions. The study found the system resilient, with 80 to 90% of turnover still settled even when all collateral lost 70% of its value. For simulation it is a worked example of cascading failure and network-flow analysis of a payment system, showing how a shock propagates through participant liquidity. It is related to the ECB macro stress testing framework record in this catalogue, which covers bank solvency, not payment liquidity.
